public_rationale: No reviewed result meets the early-resolution rule. Scaling has produced gains, including compositional generalization on controlled tasks, while other tests retain substantial gaps. Neither finding settles whether scaling alone can eventually solve a listed problem broadly. With no deadline, continued failures cannot establish the forecast.
limitations: The boundary between scaling and a new method is unclear.
A narrow benchmark reading would give greater weight to the positive compositionality result.
The search cannot establish the absence of every potentially relevant result.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Scaling will not be enough to solve the problems of understanding, compositionality, negation, and reliability in LLMs.

statement.excerpt: Scale isn’t everything, and hasn’t and won’t be enough to solve any of the problems I just listed above.

from_speaker: to solve any of the problems I just listed above
our_interpretation: Assess the future 'won't' component separately from the historical observation.
Scale means increasing model size, training data and compute within substantially the same method. Material architecture or training-method changes cannot automatically be credited to scale alone.
Solving a problem means dependable performance across varied, relevant tasks and novel cases, not success on one example or a narrow benchmark.
Because the claim says 'any', a convincing scaling-only resolution of even one listed problem could contradict it.
No deadline is supplied. Continuing failures cannot establish that scaling will never suffice.
criteria.support_condition: A general result establishing that scaling alone cannot resolve any of the listed problems under assumptions that actually cover the claimed model class.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A publicly documented, independently reproduced model or model family broadly resolves at least one listed problem, with controlled evidence attributing that resolution to scaling alone.

evidence.publisher: arXiv; Apoorv Khandelwal and Ellie Pavlick
evidence.explanation: The study reports smaller compositionality gaps at greater model sizes, but substantial remaining gaps. These finite results establish neither permanent impossibility nor broad resolution through scaling.

evidence.excerpt: Scaling model size and data enables compositional generalization.
evidence.explanation: Controlled symbolic reasoning experiments show meaningful compositional generalization from scaling, with 80% success on held-out task instances at sufficient scale. This challenges a blanket denial of scaling benefits, but does not establish broad resolution of compositionality in LLMs.

evidence.excerpt: along with architecture and optimization innovations.
evidence.explanation: OpenAI reports improved knowledge and reliability from a larger model, while explicitly identifying additional innovations. This announcement establishes neither elimination of a listed problem nor attribution to scaling alone.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: An independently reproduced result showing that scaling alone broadly resolves at least one listed problem would contradict the forecast. An applicable general impossibility result covering all listed problems could support it; further finite failures would leave it open.
